geo.summary: Az-moving was named in 0 of 15 successfully tested engine-query combinations across Perplexity, OpenAI, Claude. The reused evidence produced an AI visibility score of 0/100, with 0% mention rate and 0% citation rate. Likely contributing factors include limited owned-page answer density, limited citations of az-moving.com, and stronger third-party source visibility for competitors in the tested responses.

executive_summary: Az-moving's homepage contains meaningful trust signals - a HomeStars score, WSIB and CVOR credentials, and granular GTA service-area coverage - but the current headline, body copy, and structural choices may reduce how quickly the right visitors self-qualify and proceed to contact. The hero headline contains no geographic anchor and leads with generic descriptors that are common across the category, making it harder for a Toronto-area visitor to immediately confirm relevance. Several of the strongest trust elements (credential logos, phone number) are rendered in ways that may not be visible to all users or to text-based crawlers, limiting both human and AI-search recognition. Addressing headline clarity, trust-signal accessibility, form friction, and structured markup represents the highest-leverage opportunity to improve visitor confidence and contact rates.

ready_materials.meta_description: Az-moving provides residential and commercial moving services. Request a quote to discuss timing, service coverage and move details.

faq.question: How do I request a moving quote from Az-moving?
faq.answer: Use the website quote or contact form and share your origin, destination, preferred move date, inventory size, and any building access details.

faq.question: What details should I prepare before contacting Az-moving?
faq.answer: Prepare the pickup and drop-off addresses, preferred timing, approximate item list, stairs or elevator access, parking details, and any special handling needs.

faq.question: How should I confirm service availability for my move?
faq.answer: Request a quote with your move details so the team can confirm service coverage, timing, and any requirements specific to your building or items.

implementation_briefs.fix_title: Rewrite the H1 headline to lead with Toronto/GTA and a specific differentiator
acceptance_criteria: Done when the rendered homepage HTML contains exactly one H1 tag and its text includes a Toronto or GTA geographic reference.
Done when the H1 text references at least one specific, factually accurate differentiator (e.g., a named credential or rating platform) that appears elsewhere on the page.
Done when a browser view-source check confirms the H1 is a native H1 element, not a CSS-styled div or span.

implementation_briefs.fix_title: Add LocalBusiness and Service schema markup to the homepage
acceptance_criteria: Done when Google's Rich Results Test parses the homepage and returns a valid LocalBusiness entity with no critical errors.
Done when the JSON-LD block is present in the rendered HTML source and includes all required fields: name, address, telephone, url, and areaServed.
Done when no review-rating properties appear in the schema unless a verifiable crawlable review source is confirmed and documented.

implementation_briefs.fix_title: Make trust credentials visible as text, not only as image elements
acceptance_criteria: Done when a browser view-source of the live homepage shows a plain-text block near the credentials section naming each credential without requiring image rendering.
Done when each credential logo image has a non-empty, descriptive alt attribute visible in the HTML source.
Done when the text block is visible in a browser with images disabled or with lazy-loading blocked.

implementation_briefs.fix_title: Add an FAQ section to the homepage addressing common mover-selection questions
acceptance_criteria: Done when the homepage HTML contains at least four visible FAQ question-and-answer pairs readable without image rendering or JavaScript.
Done when Google's Rich Results Test returns a valid FAQPage entity with no critical errors for the homepage URL.
Done when every answer in the FAQ section contains only information confirmed as accurate by the business before publication.

implementation_briefs.fix_title: Fix the post-form confirmation typo and add a response-time commitment
acceptance_criteria: Done when a test form submission on the live site displays a confirmation message with 'possible' spelled correctly and no prior typo visible.
Done when the confirmation message includes a specific, non-placeholder response-time statement (e.g., a defined number of hours or 'same business day').
Done when a plain-text search of the homepage and form confirmation HTML finds zero instances of the misspelling 'posible'.
